content: The presence of friends in misfortune is a complex thing; their sympathy relieves our grief, yet it pains us to see them grieving for our sake.
author: Aristotle
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Aristotle understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How can you extend greater compassion to yourself for your own imperfections right now?
